#!/bin/bash
# Archive the logs of one service into the retention directory.

LOG_ROOT=logs
RETENTION_DIR=archives
SERVICE=$1

TMP=/tmp/archive-logs.$$
mkdir $TMP

tar czf $TMP/$SERVICE.tar.gz $LOG_ROOT/$SERVICE
mv $TMP/$SERVICE.tar.gz $RETENTION_DIR/$SERVICE-`date +%Y%m%d`.tar.gz

rm -rf $TMP/*

echo "archived $SERVICE"
# ops-logtools

Small operations repository for the log retention job.

`bin/archive-logs.sh SERVICE` packs the logs of one service from `logs/` into a dated
tarball under `archives/`. It runs from cron on the log host every night.

Archives are pruned by hand today.

#!/bin/bash
# Archive the logs of one or more services into the retention directory,
# optionally pruning old archives afterwards.
#
# Usage: archive-logs.sh [--keep-days N] SERVICE [SERVICE...]

set -euo pipefail

LOG_ROOT=logs
RETENTION_DIR=archives

usage() {
    echo "usage: ${0##*/} [--keep-days N] SERVICE [SERVICE...]" >&2
    exit 2
}

keep_days=
services=()
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
    case $1 in
        --keep-days)
            [ $# -ge 2 ] || usage
            keep_days=$2
            shift 2
            ;;
        --keep-days=*)
            keep_days=${1#*=}
            shift
            ;;
        -h|--help) usage ;;
        --) shift; services+=("$@"); break ;;
        -*) echo "unknown option: $1" >&2; usage ;;
        *) services+=("$1"); shift ;;
    esac
done

[ "${#services[@]}" -gt 0 ] || usage

if [ -n "$keep_days" ] && ! [[ $keep_days =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
    echo "--keep-days needs a non-negative integer, got: $keep_days" >&2
    exit 2
fi

# Validate everything up front so a bad name does not leave a partial run.
for svc in "${services[@]}"; do
    if ! [[ $svc =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9._-]*$ ]]; then
        echo "invalid service name: $svc" >&2
        exit 2
    fi
    if [ ! -d "$LOG_ROOT/$svc" ]; then
        echo "no such log directory: $LOG_ROOT/$svc" >&2
        exit 1
    fi
done
[ -d "$RETENTION_DIR" ] || { echo "missing directory: $RETENTION_DIR" >&2; exit 1; }

TMP=$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/archive-logs.XXXXXX")
trap 'rm -rf -- "$TMP"' EXIT

stamp=$(date +%Y%m%d)
done_list=()
for svc in "${services[@]}"; do
    tar czf "$TMP/$svc.tar.gz" -- "$LOG_ROOT/$svc"
    mv -- "$TMP/$svc.tar.gz" "$RETENTION_DIR/$svc-$stamp.tar.gz"
    done_list+=("$svc")
done

# Prune only after all new archives are in place.
pruned=0
if [ -n "$keep_days" ]; then
    while IFS= read -r -d '' old; do
        rm -f -- "$old"
        pruned=$((pruned + 1))
    done < <(find "$RETENTION_DIR" -maxdepth 1 -type f -name '*.tar.gz' \
                  -mtime +"$keep_days" -print0)
fi

summary="archived ${#done_list[@]} service(s): ${done_list[*]}"
[ -z "$keep_days" ] || summary+="; pruned $pruned archive(s) older than $keep_days days"
echo "$summary"
EOF
cat > README.md <<'EOF'
# ops-logtools

Small operations repository for the log retention job.

## Usage

    bin/archive-logs.sh [--keep-days N] SERVICE [SERVICE...]

Packs the logs of each named service from `logs/` into a dated tarball
(`archives/SERVICE-YYYYMMDD.tar.gz`). It runs from cron on the log host every night.
Run it from the repository root.

- Several services can be given in one invocation. All names are validated before
  anything is archived; an unknown service or invalid name aborts the run.
- `--keep-days N` removes `*.tar.gz` files in `archives/` older than N days (by
  modification time) once the new archives are written. Without it nothing is pruned.
- On success it prints one summary line, e.g.
  `archived 2 service(s): web db; pruned 3 archive(s) older than 30 days`.

Example:

    bin/archive-logs.sh --keep-days 30 web db
EOF
ls logs/*; cd /tmp && rm -rf t && mkdir t && cd t && cp -r /repo/evals/bash-secure-scripting/results/raw/2026-11-01/bss-01-log-archive/baseline/run-1/workspace/{logs,archives,bin} . && touch -d '40 days ago' archives/old-20200101.tar.gz && S=($(ls logs)) && bin/archive-logs.sh --keep-days 30 "${S[@]}"; ls archives; bin/archive-logs.sh ../x; echo rc=$?

content.text:
I've changed `bin/archive-logs.sh` to take several services, accept `--keep-days N`, and print a one-line summary. I also updated the README. I tested it on a copy of the repo in `/tmp`: `bin/archive-logs.sh --keep-days 30 api web` archived both services and removed a 40-day-old test archive. A path-style name (`../x`) was rejected with exit code 2.

Usage is `bin/archive-logs.sh [--keep-days N] SERVICE [SERVICE...]`. A successful run prints one line like `archived 2 service(s): api web; pruned 1 archive(s) older than 30 days`. The `pruned` part appears only when `--keep-days` is given.

- **Pruning scope:** `--keep-days` removes every `*.tar.gz` in `archives/` older than N days by modification time, not just the services named in that run. It runs only after all the new archives are written. Without the option nothing is deleted.
- **Validation:** Every service name and log directory is checked before anything is archived. An unknown service or an invalid name aborts the run with nothing written.
- **Stricter than before:** I also tightened the script beyond what you asked.
  - It now fails on any error instead of carrying on.
  - It quotes its variables and uses a safe temporary directory.
  - Names with slashes or a leading `-` are rejected.
  - A missing `archives/` directory is an error.

The script still has to be run from the repo root, as before. Because of that, I noted it in the README.
